note: Questions from the CBSE Class X English (Language and Literature) board exam 2023, Q.P. code 2/1/1, published by CBSE at cbse.gov.in. Where a question shows a chart or picture, the official version for visually impaired candidates (or the table as text) is used. Q3(vi) is left out because its answer is open to dispute. Model answers are written for this portal and are not CBSE's official marking scheme.

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Read the passage given below :
(1) If you're like most kids, you may love snow. Not only can it get you out of school, but it's also fun to play with. Who doesn't love to sled and build snowmen ? Snow can also be dangerous, too. You may have heard your parents talk about how difficult it can be to drive in snow. Car accidents aren't the only dangers created by snow. If you're ever skiing in the mountains, you'll want to be aware of avalanches. An avalanche is a sudden flow of snow down a slope, such as a mountain. The amount of snow in an avalanche will vary based on many things, but it can be such a huge pile that it can bury the bottom of a slope in dozens of feet of snow.
(2) Avalanches can be caused by many things. Some of them are natural. For example, new snow or rain can cause built up snow to loosen and fall down the side of a mountain. Earthquakes and the movement of animals have also been known to cause avalanches. Artificial triggers can also cause avalanches. For example, snowmobiles, skiers, gunshots and explosives have all been known to cause avalanches. Avalanches usually occur during the winter and spring, when snowfall is greatest. As they are dangerous to any living beings in their path, avalanches have destroyed forests, roads, railroads and even entire towns.
(3) Warning signs exist that allow experts to predict – and often prevent – avalanches from occurring. When over a foot of fresh snow falls, experts know to be on the lookout for avalanches. Explosives can be used in places with massive snow build-ups to trigger smaller avalanches that don't pose a danger to persons or property. When deadly avalanches do occur, the moving snow can quickly reach over 80 miles per hour. Skiers caught in such avalanches can be buried under dozens of feet of snow. While it's possible to dig out of such avalanches, not all are able to escape.
(4) If you get tossed about by an avalanche and find yourself buried under many feet of snow, you might not have a true sense of which way is up and which way is down. Some avalanche victims have tried to dig their way out, only to find that they were upside down and digging themselves farther under the snow rather than to the top ! Experts suggest that people caught in an avalanche try to "swim" to the top of the moving snow to stay close to the surface. Once the avalanche stops, do your best to dig around you to create a space for air, so you can breathe easier. Then, do your best to figure out which way is up and dig in that direction to reach the surface and signal rescuers.

Answer the questions (1 mark each) :
(i) Avalanche can be caused by : (a) new snow or rain (b) heavy winds (c) high altitude (d) global warming
(ii) Comment on the warning signs which allow experts to predict avalanches, in two sentences.
(iii) Mention two reasons which destroyed the natural scenery.
(iv) Select the option that conveys the opposite of 'massive' : (a) tiny (b) lengthy (c) bulky (d) extensive
(v) The writer will agree with which statement (paragraph 4) ? (a) People caught in the avalanche can try to swim to the top. (b) Put on an oxygen mask. (c) Digging is not possible. (d) Should not come close to the surface.
(vi) Select the option that corresponds to the relation in : 'You may not have an idea of which way is up and which way is down.' (a) The crowd will gather at Gate No. 1 and disperse from Gate No. 2. (b) Due to the torrential rain, there was a heavy flooding. (c) The guest felt uneasy and uncomfortable watching the child's performance. (d) The more the effort, the bigger the gain.
(vii) Which does not trigger an avalanche ? (a) Earthquakes (b) Snow fall (c) Rain (d) Plastic waste
(viii) Complete : Explosives can be used in places ______.
(ix) The word 'deadly' in paragraph 3 most nearly means : (a) likely to cause death (b) harmful (c) very boring (d) scary
(x) Select the most suitable title : (a) Avalanches (b) Adventure with Snow (c) Ice Games (d) Calamity
questions.solution: (i) (a). (ii) When over a foot of fresh snow falls, experts watch out for avalanches. They may use explosives where a lot of snow has built up to set off small, harmless avalanches. (iii) Avalanches, which destroyed forests, roads and towns; they can be triggered naturally (new snow or rain, earthquakes) or by people (skiers, snowmobiles, gunshots, explosives). (iv) (a) tiny. (v) (a). (vi) (a): both show opposites (up/down; gather/disperse). (vii) (d). (viii) with massive snow build-ups, to trigger smaller avalanches that don't endanger people or property. (ix) (a). (x) (a) Avalanches.

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Read the passage given below :
(1) Increasing traffic congestion every year is causing increasing air pollution, wasting time and productivity and diverse respiratory diseases. Moreover, the cost of solving or reducing traffic congestion is enormous. However, neglecting the traffic jam problem would increase the social problems among citizens.
(2) The number of vehicles has increased considerably in the city in the past five years. Due to this increase, the city roads witness frequent traffic congestions, but above all, the vehicles emitting pollutants are affecting the environment adversely.
(3) The Capital's vehicular population saw an addition of more than five lakh vehicles last year, registering an increase of over 4%, according to the Delhi Economic Survey 2020-21.
(4) In spite of the largest road network, through metro and bus services in major cities the transport system is not being able to keep pace with the growing demand. Consequently, more and more people use their private vehicles, leading to increased congestion on the roads. In spite of these challenges people in India prefer road travel over air and other means of travel. Citizens of Delhi/NCR have, time and again, pondered over the possibilities of how to reduce the traffic congestion in the city, especially during the peak hours. People should use public transport, the government must increase the facilities of public transport, people should avoid the unnecessary collection of vehicles and should use carpool and vehicle sharing.
(5) What is required is proper implementation of corrective measures by citizens to get an organized traffic management system.

Answer the questions (1 mark each) :
(i) Infer one reason, based on paragraph 1, why reducing traffic congestion is not easy.
(ii) The reasons for increased traffic congestion are : 1. use of private vehicles 2. increase in demand for cars 3. inability to keep pace with population control 4. travelling by public transport 5. emission of pollutants. (a) 4, 5 (b) 1, 5 (c) 1, 2 (d) 2, 3
(iii) Complete the analogy with a word from the passage : organized : chaotic : : lowest : ______
(iv) The vehicles emit pollutants which affect ______ badly.
(v) Complete : Use of public transport will reduce ______.
(vi) Methods of reducing traffic congestion : 1. start car pooling 2. add electric buses 3. increase in public modes of transport 4. increase car collection points 5. increase taxation. (a) 1, 4, 5 (b) 3, 5 (c) 2, 3, 4 (d) 1, 3
(vii) What is required to get an organized traffic management system ?
(viii) Give the reasons for increase in vehicular congestion.
(ix) There are ______ consequences of increasing vehicular congestion. (a) beneficial (b) adverse (c) implicit (d) explicit
(x) Substitute the word 'pondered' with ONE WORD similar in meaning : Citizens of Delhi/NCR have time and time again pondered over the possibilities of how to reduce traffic congestion.
questions.solution: (i) The cost of solving or reducing traffic congestion is enormous. (ii) (c) 1, 2. (iii) peak (from 'peak hours'). (iv) the environment. (v) traffic congestion (and air pollution). (vi) (d) 1, 3. (vii) Proper implementation of corrective measures by citizens. (viii) The number of vehicles has risen sharply, and public transport cannot keep pace with demand, so more people use private vehicles. (ix) (b) adverse. (x) considered / thought (over) / reflected.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Reena always ______ the truth.
questions.solution: A habitual action with a singular subject takes the simple present 'speaks'.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Select the correct option to fill in the blank : Bread and butter ______ my favourite breakfast.
questions.solution: 'Bread and butter' is thought of as one dish, so it takes a singular verb: 'is'.

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Ravi : "Reena, lend me hundred rupees." Reena : "I don't have it right now, but I will arrange it for you."
Ravi asked Reena to lend him hundred rupees, to which Reena replied that ______.
questions.solution: she didn't have it right then, but she would arrange it for him.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Select the option that identifies the error and supplies the correction : I can run fast when I was young.
questions.solution: The time is past ('when I was young'), so 'can' becomes 'could'.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Complete the narrative : Heena ______ from fever since last Sunday.
questions.solution: An action that began in the past and is still going on ('since last Sunday') takes the present perfect continuous.

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Mother : Why are you looking so worried ? Daughter : My exams are approaching.
In response to the question of the mother, the daughter replied that ______.
questions.solution: her exams were approaching.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Identify the error and supply the correction : The ship Titanic and her fate continues to fascinate the imagination of the people.
questions.solution: Error: continues. Correction: continue (two subjects joined by 'and').

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Ritu and Randeep are talking. Report Ritu's question. Ritu : Where are you going ?
Ritu asked ______.
questions.solution: Randeep where he was going.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Complete the slogan : ______ smile and pass it to others.
questions.solution: 'Always smile and pass it to others' — an adverb is needed before the verb 'smile'.

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Anil : Where are you going ? Sanjeev : To the airport. Anil : May I drop you there as I'm going in that direction ?
Anil asked Sanjeev where he was going and offered to drop him as ______.
options: he could be going in that direction
he would be going in the direction
he is going in the direction
he was going in that direction
questions.solution: 'I'm going' becomes 'he was going' in reported speech.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Identify the error in the newspaper headline : Attractive packages for different Tourist destination – Mizoram, Kashmir, Kerala, Goa.
questions.solution: Error: destination. Correction: destinations.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: You are pained to see that in your city, there is no proper arrangement for cleaning of drains. There are heaps of accumulated garbage and stagnant water. Write a letter to the Municipal Commissioner of your city complaining about the same as there is a fear of outbreak of disease. You are Alka/Ashish. (Word limit 100–120)
questions.solution: Format (1 mark): sender's address, date, The Municipal Commissioner, subject (Uncleaned drains and garbage in our area), salutation, close, name. Content (2 marks): drains are clogged and overflowing; heaps of garbage and stagnant water; foul smell, mosquitoes and flies; fear of diseases such as dengue, malaria and cholera; repeated complaints ignored; request for regular cleaning, garbage collection and spraying of insecticide. Organisation and accuracy (2 marks): formal tone, clear paragraphs, correct language.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: The authorities have been claiming that the roads in your town have been relaid and repaired. But no such work done is seen. Write a letter to the editor of a local newspaper expressing your concern at the present situation and giving suggestions to resolve the problem, in 100–120 words. You are Prabhu/Parvati of Vivek Vihar, Delhi.
questions.solution: Format (1 mark): sender's address, date, The Editor and newspaper name, subject (Poor condition of roads despite claims of repair), salutation, close, name. Content (2 marks): authorities claim roads are repaired but potholes and broken stretches remain; accidents, traffic jams, dust and damage to vehicles; especially risky in the rains; suggestions: an inquiry into the claimed work, quality checks, quick repair with accountability, regular maintenance and a public complaint helpline. Organisation and accuracy (2 marks).

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
The chart below displays details regarding online activity (%) for four age groups in six categories. Write an analytical paragraph in about 100 words.
Activity : Teens / 20s / 30s / 40s
News : 76 / 71 / 72 / 78
Downloads : 85 / 55 / 35 / 25
Buying a product : 44 / 66 / 67 / 69
Online games : 88 / 55 / 36 / 28
Searching for a product : 0 / 77 / 81 / 85
Searching for people : 6 / 33 / 22 / 21
questions.solution: Introduction: the table shows how four age groups use the internet. Analysis: reading news is popular with all ages (71–78%). Teenagers lead in online games (88%) and downloads (85%), and these fall steadily with age (28% and 25% in the 40s). Searching for and buying products rise with age: no teenager searches for products, but 85% of people in their 40s do, and buying rises from 44% to 69%. Searching for people is highest among people in their 20s (33%). Conclusion: young people use the internet mainly for entertainment, while older users use it for shopping and information. Marks: format and content 3, accuracy 2.

questions.subject: English
questions.text:
Rehanna is to write an analytical paragraph on 'Hazards of Smoking'. Using your own ideas and the information given below, write the paragraph in 100–120 words.
Smoking – drains out income of an average earner – affect health badly – vital organs are affected – harmful for passive smokers – need to educate people – role of media in creating awareness.
questions.solution: Introduction: smoking is a harmful habit. Analysis: it drains the income of an average earner, money that could be spent on food, education or health; it damages health badly, affecting the lungs, heart and other vital organs and causing cancer and breathing problems; it also harms passive smokers, including children, who breathe in the smoke. Conclusion: people must be educated about these dangers, and the media can play a big role through campaigns and advertisements. Marks: content 3, accuracy 2.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: From the Diary of Anne Frank
questions.text:
Read the extract and answer the questions (1 mark each) :
Let me put this more clearly, since no one will believe that a thirteen-year old girl is completely alone in this world. And I'm not. I have loving parents and a sixteen years old sister, and there are almost thirty people I can call friends. I have a family, loving aunts and a good house. No, on the surface I seem to have everything, except my one true friend. All I think about when I am with friends is having a good time. I can't bring myself to talk about anything, but ordinary everyday things.
(i) On the surface, it appears that Anne the thirteen year old girl ______.
(ii) How can we infer that the speaker felt alone in the world ? (a) She had a family of many people. (b) She had loving parents. (c) She had thirty friends. (d) She craves for a true friend.
(iii) Anne and her friends talked about ______. (a) their problematic parents (b) their financial problems (c) common everyday things (d) the commuting problems
(iv) Complete the analogy with a suitable word from the text : alone : friends : : nothing : ______
(v) The idiom 'bring myself' in the extract means : (a) to do something willingly (b) to do something unwillingly (c) a charitable act (d) an involuntary act
questions.solution: (i) has everything (loving parents, a sister, friends and a good house). (ii) (d). (iii) (c). (iv) everything. (v) (a) to do something willingly (she cannot make herself talk about anything deeper).

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: Footprints without Feet: Footprints without Feet
questions.text:
Read the extract and answer the questions (1 mark each) :
Mrs. Hall almost fell down the stairs in hysterics. She was convinced that the room was haunted by spirits and that the stranger had somehow caused these to enter into her furniture.
(i) Mrs. Hall tripped because : (a) the floor was oily (b) she was standing on a chair (c) she was in a state of panic (d) the door was slammed
(ii) Mrs. Hall suspected everything in the room was put under a spell of witchcraft by ______.
(iii) Fill in the blank with one word : Mrs. Hall was afraid that spirits had entered ______.
(iv) The feeling of Mrs. Hall can be best described as : (1) stunned (2) happy (3) awestruck (4) nervous (5) outraged (6) agitated. (a) 2 and 4 (b) 3 and 6 (c) 5 and 6 (d) 1 and 6
(v) 'Spirits' in the above lines means the same as : (a) ghosts (b) conscience (c) ego (d) attitude
questions.solution: (i) (c). (ii) the stranger (Griffin). (iii) furniture. (iv) (d) stunned and agitated. (v) (a) ghosts.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: How to Tell Wild Animals
questions.text:
Read the extract and answer the questions (1 mark each) :
Though to distinguish beasts of prey
A novice might nonplus,
The crocodiles you always may
Tell from the Hyena thus :
Hyenas come with merry smiles;
But if they weep they're crocodiles.
(i) Crocodiles can be identified by their : (a) tears (b) attitude (c) smiles (d) attacks
(ii) True or False : Hyenas are famous for weeping.
(iii) 'Novice' in line 2 means the same as : (a) learner (b) beast (c) tender foot (d) beginner
(iv) In this extract the poet has presented two different behavioural traits of animals. They are ______.
(v) The poet uses 'A novice might nonplus' instead of 'the novice might get confused'. How does this usage impact the poem ? (a) adds an incorrect option (b) it is associated with beasts (c) it rhymes and adds humour (d) it simplifies the meaning
questions.solution: (i) (a) tears. (ii) False (hyenas are known for their 'laughing' sound). (iii) (d) beginner. (iv) hyenas smile (laugh) merrily, while crocodiles weep (shed tears). (v) (c).

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: A Tiger in the Zoo
questions.text:
Read the extract and answer the questions (1 mark each) :
He stalks in his vivid stripes
The few steps of his cage,
On pads of velvet quiet,
In his quiet rage
He should be lurking in shadow
Sliding through long grass
Near the water hole
Where plump deer pass.
(i) Complete : The vivid stripes refer to the ______.
(ii) Which word from the extract is the opposite of 'loud' ?
(iii) The phrase 'pads of velvet' means : (a) neck (b) tail (c) skin (d) paws
(iv) True or False : The confinement of the cramped space of the cage has restricted the tiger's steps.
(v) The tiger should be lurking in shadow ______. (a) to catch its prey (b) as the cage was dark (c) as the velvet was quiet (d) as he was in a rage
questions.solution: (i) bright stripes on the tiger's body (skin). (ii) quiet. (iii) (d) paws. (iv) True. (v) (a) to catch its prey.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: Glimpses of India – Tea from Assam
questions.text: What did Pranjol and Rajvir do during the journey ? Why ? Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: Pranjol was buried in a detective novel, because he had grown up on a tea estate and the scenery was nothing new to him. Rajvir looked out of the window, admiring the green paddy fields, forests and tea gardens, because it was his first visit to Assam and he was fascinated by tea plantations.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: A Letter to God
questions.text: Who read the letter sent by Lencho ? What did he do then ? Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: The postmaster read the letter. He laughed at first but was moved by Lencho's faith in God. Not wanting to shake that faith, he decided to answer it; he collected money from his employees and friends, gave part of his own salary, and sent about seventy pesos signed 'God'.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: Glimpses of India – Coorg
questions.text: Where is Coorg located ? Write any two characteristics of the people of Coorg. Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: Coorg (Kodagu) is the smallest district of Karnataka, midway between Mysore and the coastal town of Mangalore. Its people, the Kodavus, are known for their martial traditions and bravery (the Coorg Regiment is among the most decorated in the army) and for their warm hospitality; they also tell stories of valour.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: The Tale of Custard the Dragon
questions.text: How does the poem 'The Tale of Custard The Dragon' differ from the traditional ballad ? Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: It is written in ballad form, with a story, rhyme and rhythm, but it is humorous rather than serious. Instead of a brave hero, the 'cowardly' dragon Custard turns out to be the hero who kills the pirate, while the boastful kitten, mouse and dog run away. It mocks heroism playfully.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: The Sermon at Benares
questions.text: What does the Buddha say about the world ? Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: The Buddha says that the world is afflicted with death and decay. Everyone who is born must die, just as ripe fruit falls and earthen vessels break. The wise do not grieve, knowing this is the law of the world; grieving only brings pain, and peace comes by giving up lamentation and selfishness.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: Footprints without Feet: The Thief's Story
questions.text: Why does Anil not hand over Hari Singh to the police ? Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: Anil realised Hari Singh had stolen the money and then returned it (the notes were still damp from the rain). Kind and forgiving, he did not want to ruin the boy's chance to change. Instead he gave him a fifty-rupee note as payment and promised to keep teaching him, showing his trust.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: Footprints without Feet: The Making of a Scientist
questions.text: What opinion did Mr. Weiherer, Ebright's Social Science teacher have about him ? Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: Mr Weiherer said Richard Ebright was not only very intelligent but had a burning desire to win, and to win for the right reasons. He wanted to do the best job he could and not just win; he was competitive and hardworking, but fair.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: Footprints without Feet: A Triumph of Surgery
questions.text: What was Mr. Herriot's strict advice ? Did Mrs. Pumphrey agree to his advice ? Answer in 40–50 words.
questions.solution: Herriot strictly advised Mrs Pumphrey to cut down Tricki's sweets and rich food and give him more exercise. She did not follow it: she could not resist Tricki's pleading and kept giving him extra treats, so he grew worse and finally had to be taken to Herriot's surgery.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: Madam Rides the Bus
questions.text: Whenever we want to achieve something, difficulties always come in our way. What did Valli have to do to go and ride in a bus ? Answer in 100–120 words.
questions.solution: Valli, an eight-year-old girl, longed to ride the bus to town. She carefully listened to conversations about the bus journey, found out the fare (thirty paise each way) and how long it took. She saved every coin she could, resisting the temptation to buy peppermints, toys and balloons, and even skipped a ride on the merry-go-round. She chose the afternoon, when her mother slept, so she could go and return without anyone knowing. On the bus she confidently paid her fare, refused to be treated like a child and enjoyed the view. Her planning, patience, sacrifice and courage helped her overcome every difficulty.

questions.subject: English
questions.chapter: First Flight: The Sermon at Benares
questions.text: Through the story of Kisa Gotami, what did the Buddha try to preach to the common man ? Answer in 100–120 words.
questions.solution: Kisa Gotami's only son died, and in grief she went from house to house seeking medicine to bring him back. The Buddha asked her to bring a handful of mustard seed from a house where no one had lost a child, husband, parent or friend. She found no such house and realised that death comes to everyone. Through her, the Buddha taught that death is common to all and the world is subject to decay. Grieving only increases pain and harms the body; the wise do not grieve but accept the law of nature. One who overcomes sorrow and gives up selfishness and lamentation attains peace.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Education is always a great asset in the life of a woman. How did Bholi, an educated girl, face the challenge posed by Bishamber's greed ? Answer in 100–120 words.
questions.solution: Bholi, once a timid girl who stammered, gained confidence and self-respect through school and her kind teacher. Her marriage was fixed with Bishamber, an old, lame man, because of her pockmarked face. At the wedding, seeing her face, he demanded a dowry of five thousand rupees, and her father, humiliated, gave it. Bholi then refused to marry such a greedy, mean man. She threw away the garland, spoke without stammering, and declared she would serve her parents in their old age and teach at the same school. Education gave her the courage to stand up against injustice and choose her own future.

questions.subject: English
questions.text: Those who are satisfied with what they have are happy in life. Those who aspire more than what they can afford ruin their life. Matilda was one such person. If she were content with her life she would have led a happy life. Elaborate on the basis of the chapter 'The Necklace.' Answer in 100–120 words.
questions.solution: Matilda Loisel was pretty but always unhappy with her simple life as a clerk's wife; she dreamed of wealth and luxury. When invited to a ball, she was not content with what she had: she made her husband spend his savings on a dress and borrowed a diamond necklace from Mme Forestier to look rich. She lost the necklace, and to replace it the couple borrowed thirty-six thousand francs and spent ten years in poverty and hard labour, ageing her terribly. Finally she learned the necklace was fake. Had she been content and honest, she would have avoided this suffering and lived happily.
